_comment: Copy to data/sources.json. One entry per source; 'kind' picks the adapter.
Set enabled=false to park a source without deleting it.
role_filter at the top level is the default every source inherits: a regex
the job TITLE must match to be ingested. The one shipped in sources.py is
an IT example - replace it with your own field. Setting it to null on a
source accepts everything from that source, which is what you want for an
employer board where you would take any opening.
location_filter does the same against the location string. Pair it with
role_filter: null on a single-employer board to mean 'anything, near me'.
IMPORTANT: this file is read at runtime and OVERRIDES the defaults in
sources.py. Changing DEFAULT_ROLE_FILTER in code does nothing once this
file exists. That has caught people out.

sources._: Remote job boards. No token needed, just a search phrase.
ATS boards. The token is the company slug in the board's URL:
Workday. tenant and site come out of the careers URL:
Paylocity recruiting boards. The token is the UUID in the board URL.
NeoGov / governmentjobs.com. agency is the slug in the portal URL:
Frontline/AppliTrack school district boards. Give it the URL you see.
sources.__: salary_schedule is optional: where the district publishes its pay
sources.___: scale. Used when a posting states no pay of its own.

sources._: HireTrue / ce3 boards, used by several US state governments.
sources.__: host, board_key and board_id are all visible in the board's URL.

sources._: Advanced Classifieds & Directory Pro - small regional job boards.
Career pages with no feed at all, watched by changedetection.io.
sources.__: Add the watches in its own UI and tag them; this reads that tag.
